title: Surface Cues Over Structure: Probing LLM Behavior on Brain Connectivity Graphs
abstract: arXiv:2611.26913v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) provides a noninvasive view of functional interactions across the brain, which can be represented as connectivity graphs for neurological disease analysis. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being paired with such representations, yet it remains unclear whether they genuinely reason over the underlying connectivity or simply respond to surface-level cues that may trigger learned priors. We probe this question through a controlled study of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) diagnosis from resting-state functional connectivity, isolating one factor at a time to determine what drives an LLM's predictions on brain connectivity graphs. Across six models, from small open-weight LLMs to a proprietary one, the same pattern holds: the results provide little evidence that predictions are consistently grounded in subject-specific connectivity. translated_title: 表面线索优于结构：探究大语言模型在脑连接图上的行为
translated_abstract: 静息态功能磁共振成像为大脑间的功能交互提供了无创的观察视角，可以将其表示为连接图，用于神经系统疾病分析。大语言模型越来越多地与这类表示相结合，然而尚不清楚它们是真正对底层连接结构进行推理，还是仅仅对可能触发已学习先验的表面线索做出反应。我们通过对静息态功能连接的注意力缺陷/多动障碍（ADHD）诊断的受控研究来探究这一问题，每次只隔离一个因素，以确定是什么驱动大语言模型在脑连接图上的预测。在从小型开源权重LLM到专有模型的六个模型中，同样的模式均成立：结果几乎没有提供预测始终基于受试者特定连接的证据。大脑区域名称……
tldr: 该研究通过受控实验发现，大语言模型在基于脑功能连接图进行ADHD诊断时，主要依赖表面线索（如脑区名称）而非真正对受试者特定的连接结构进行推理。
en_tdlr: Through controlled experiments on ADHD diagnosis from resting-state functional connectivity, this study reveals that LLMs rely on surface cues such as brain region names rather than genuinely reasoning over subject-specific connectivity structures.
